To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the market system is a political creation and that the double movement is a permanent feature of the market system.
the market system cannot be sustained without government intervention, and that the government's intervention is designed to amelioratethe destructive consequences ofthe market system.

1. the self-regulating labor market, the cornerstone of classical economics, was not created by the market itself but by government intervention; 2. the market could not survive for long without government intervention; 3. government intervention in the market was not a response to economic failure but was an essential element of the market; 4. the market system required the denial of life outside the market;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and economic effects of the self-regulation of the market, with the extent to which these effects are resented, and with the efforts made to combat them

the double movement, that is the two-fold process of the extension of the market organization into areas previously regulated by non-market institutions and the counter-movement which sets out to arrest the process of the increasing subjection of social goals to the impersonal forces of the market (132).
the development of the market economy, and the double movement that has always opposed it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the market system is not self-adjusting, that it cannot automatically work toward a state of rest, that it constantly needs the presence of a coercive mechanism to prevent it from destroying itself; but, at the same time, that this mechanism is not a part of the system, but an outside force, which, while it is indispensable, cannot, for this very reason, be integrated into the system without destroying its own character.
the market system was the outcome of a double movement.
the self-regulating system of the market destroyed the economic and social equilibrium without being able to build up any other in its place.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the market system was not self-regulating but required government intervention.
the market economy is a system of production and consumption, and the market system is a system of distribution and exchange.
the market system was created and sustained by a double movement: a movement to establish a self-regulating market and a counter-movement to mitigate its worst effects (3).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the market economy is not self-sustaining.
we need to do a better job in the future of making sure that our policies are not just about making the market more efficient but that they are actually making people's lives better.
the double movement has been in operation since the emergence ofthe market system, and the double movement is the key to understanding the emergence and persistenceofthe welfare state.
